I am not sure what your rational is for first running PLM/FLN on the
whole data set and then redoing it on a subset. What is your
statistical model/algorithm you're trying fit?

In general, very few models/methods in aroma.affymetrix provide a way
to specify a subset of arrays. One reason for this the large risk for
conflicting/overwriting result files, which is what you are
experiencing. Instead, the idea is to have the result sets being
separated from each others by outputting them in different
directories. Then, if you later want to merge them together in a
downstream analysis, that can be done using the append() method of
AffymetrixCelSet.

To output your the PLM results for the XX and the XY samples in
different directories, just add a tag to each of them, e.g.

dsNXX <- extract(dsN,xxIdxs);
plm <- RmaCnPlm(dsNXX, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, tags=c("*","XX"))
fit(plm);
cesXX <- getChipEffectSet(plm);

dsNXY <- extract(dsN,xyIdxs);
plm <- RmaCnPlm(dsNXY, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, tags=c("*","XY"))
fit(plm);
cesXY <- getChipEffectSet(plm);

# Merge the chip-effect sets.
ces <- cesXX;
append(ces, cesXY);
print(ces);

Note that when you merge the sets, the first set (here 'cesXX') will
be the one specifying the name and the tags. To override this, you
can use:

setAlias(ces, 'MyMergedDataset')

to change the name. It's been a while, but I think you can use
setTags() to change the tags. Default is "*" which expands to
whatever the pathname says it is.

Then, if you do:

fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces);
process(fln);

The output data set will contain normalized data files from the above
two sets with a name and tags as you specified.
